summary: IDS feed s157_double is degraded: 8.4% of frames exceed IDS 1518B MTU and are dropped by NIC, plus 2.56 Gbps microbursts overload the 1 Gbps IDS port (256% capacity). Both cause silent packet loss and detection gaps.

findings.root_cause: Upstream network is using jumbo frames up to 8058 bytes and packet broker is forwarding them unchanged to a standard 1518B IDS port without jumbo-frame support or MTU normalization.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC drops 137 of 1634 frames (8.4%) that exceed 1518B. IDS requires full payload so it loses entire flows/payloads, creating blind spots for exploit and malware detection; slicing/trimming is not an option.

recommended_fix.why: Tool needs full payload so do not slice. Either enable jumbo frames (e.g., 9000B) end-to-end on broker egress and IDS NIC, or enforce 1518B MTU upstream with proper fragmentation to prevent NIC drops.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is aggregating too much traffic onto a single 1 Gbps IDS port without load-balancing or rate-control, producing 1ms microbursts up to 2.56 Gbps.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS port is overrun at 256% capacity across 6 intervals, causing random packet drops, TCP reassembly failures, missed signatures and degraded detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute feed via broker load-balancing across 3x 1G IDS ports or upgrade to 10G to keep peak utilization below 80% and prevent burst drops.
